text:
anya: heads-up — p99 jumped ~3x on shared-gpu-usw2 around 09:07. Seeing tenant-42 as common factor. Initial read: KV-cache eviction storms + kernel fallbacks to fp32 under mem pressure. Anyone on this?

infra-bot: alert: high-latency detected on pool shared-gpu-usw2 — triggered 09:06:42 — incident id inc-20260317-42

simon: can you drop links to dashboard + profiler? cudatop or runtime traces would help.

anya: dashboard: https://perf.redwood/r/USW2/shared-gpu (short link). Logs from control-plane: `sgpctl logs --tenant tenant-42 --since 2026-03-17T09:00Z` show repeated `kv_cache:evict` bursts around 09:06-09:08 correlating with latency spikes.

devon: quick sampling from runtime profiler (snip):
```
p99_latency_ms: 940 -> baseline 320
kv_cache_evictions: 1187 in 120s
avg_kv_hit_rate: 0.17
kernel_fallbacks_to_fp32: 87
gpu_mem_usage_peak: 93%
```
fallback log lines: `kernel_selector: quantized_kernel unavailable -> falling back to fp32 due to activation_mem+kv_cache > threshold`

jules: was tenant-42 running a fan-out batch pattern? small requests but many concurrent streams can thrash KV cache.

ops-sre: we saw a sudden client-side spike from tenant-42 at 09:05:57 — they ramped to ~48 concurrent requests, many ~800-1200 token requests. Bursty token footprint.

simon: if kernel selection is falling back under mem pressure, that explains CPU-side latency increase too. Do we have per-tenant mem accounting to enforce a soft cap?

anya: currently only per-pool accounting. We can add per-tenant KV reservation but need a quick mitigation first.

devon: root cause draft: tenant burst pushes KV cache > eviction threshold which increases cache churn reducing hit-rate. More cache thrash -> more activations retained -> memory spikes -> kernel_selector sees incompatible quant path -> fallback to fp32 kernels (higher memory & latency). It's a cascade.

simon: suggested short-term mitigations: 1) apply per-tenant concurrency cap 2) tune aggressive cold-prefix eviction 3) add token-rate limits on the ingress LB. Thoughts?

jules: +1. Also could we change kernel selection heuristic to prefer quantized kernels even if it requires rejecting batches that would overflow? Prefer graceful requeue instead of fallback.

ops-sre: applied per-tenant concurrency limit for tenant-42 at 09:25 (10 concurrent slots) and throttled token-rate at the edge. Observed p99 returning to ~330ms by 09:28. :thumbsup:

anya: good. For medium-term: devon, can you run a replay with tenant-42 traces against a canary runtime that changes kernel selection to reject oversize batches instead of fallback? Capture p50/p95/p99 and KV-hit behavior.

devon: yep — will run: `sgpctl replay --tenant tenant-42 --since 2026-03-17T09:00Z --compare canary-kernel-selection` and post results. Expect ~5% tail improvement if requeue works.

simon: also please profile memory breakdown per allocation type (KV cache vs activation vs kernels) — want percentages.

devon: initial breakdown from sample run: `kv_cache: 55%, activations: 30%, kernel_workspace: 15%` — this matches the eviction->fallback story.

jules: file an action ticket for formal per-tenant memory accounting and hard token/concurrency quotas in shared pools. We need fairness guarantees.

infra-bot: perf-issue-ticket created: IR-912 (priority P2) — assigned eng-runtime. ETA 72h.

anya: thanks all. Follow-ups: devon posts replay metrics in this thread, simon + jules to propose config defaults for per-tenant limits, ops-sre to propose runtime safe-fallback policy.

ops-sre: ack — monitoring alert rule updated to include per-tenant kv_eviction_rate threshold so we auto-throttle on recurrence.

devon: posting short follow-up later today with full profiler dump and canary comparison.

anya: great — closing loop once replay numbers are in.
